A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PatchScaler, and their main text, equations, tables and figures are readable. However, v1 includes Appendices A–C, whereas v4 ends after the references and refers to supplementary architecture details, ablations and SUPIR comparisons that are not supplied. Those parts cannot be fully matched.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluations on LSDIR-Test, RealSR and RealSet110, runtime measurements, prompt and sampling ablations, and additional appendix analyses.

after.justification: V4 reports original benchmark results, runtime comparisons, sampling and prompt analyses, and a new experiment applying GRM and PGS to StableSR.

M1.justification: The core GRM–PGS–Patch-DiT pipeline and retrieved texture guidance remain intact. V4 Section 4.3 introduces a training-free adaptation combining GRM and PGS with StableSR. Algorithm 1 restates the existing retrieval procedure, and time-dependent cross-attention scaling was already described in v1 Appendix A.3.

E1.justification: V4 adds HQ-50K alongside LSDIR for restoration-model training; v1 trained those modules on LSDIR. The evaluation datasets remain LSDIR-Test, RealSR and RealSet110, and the reference-memory source datasets remain unchanged. This expands training data within the existing super-resolution task.

E2.justification: V4 Tables 1–2 add the one-step methods SinSR and OSEDiff to the comparison, substantially extending the efficiency comparison beyond the earlier multi-step methods. SinSR was cited but not evaluated in v1. The main qualitative comparison also adds OSEDiff and omits LDM and PASD. The mentioned SUPIR comparison cannot be verified without the missing supplement.

E3.justification: V1 reports 50K iterations for GRM and the texture classifier, followed by 500K for Patch-DiT and its texture encoder. V4 instead reports 700K PatchScaler iterations, with GRM participating during the first 100K. V4 also introduces the StableSR transfer protocol with 64×64 latent patches. Its main runtime comparison retains only 512→2048, whereas v1 also reports 256→1024.

E4.justification: V4 Table 3 and Figure 7 add a substantive test of PGS portability through StableSR with and without the adaptation. Figure 6 expands the joint intermediate-timestep and sampling-step sweep beyond v1 Table 4. The confidence-map examples in v4 Figure 3 reuse examples from v1 Appendix Figure 7 and are not a new analysis. Other appendix analyses cannot be matched to the missing v4 supplement.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The learned confidence maps and confidence bins describe reconstruction difficulty, not statistical uncertainty in reported results.

E6.justification: PatchScaler scores are replaced across all three benchmarks. For example, RealSet110 ManIQA/CLIPIQA/MUSIQ change from 0.5040/0.8038/68.27 to 0.5442/0.8213/70.97. These accompany revised training and cannot establish a controlled cross-version gain. V4 adds one-step baseline results and StableSR+PGS results, including 8.53 seconds versus StableSR's 35.22 seconds. PatchScaler's existing 2048-output runtime remains 3.41 seconds.

T1.justification: The shared GRM loss, confidence grouping and diffusion derivation in Equations 1–7 are substantively retained; Algorithm 1 formalizes previously described retrieval. However, v1 Appendix A.2 supplies the explicit patch-conditioned denoising objective in Equation 8, whose counterpart cannot be checked because v4's architectural supplement is unavailable. Its removal, relocation or revision remains unresolved.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same principal contributions: patch-adaptive acceleration, retrieved texture guidance and favorable reconstruction quality with efficient inference. The ResShift comparison changes from a stated 77.1% speedup to approximately 0.23× runtime, expressing the same underlying result. Stronger adjectives do not establish a different core claim.

C2.justification: V4 adds explanations for choosing three difficulty groups and interprets PGS as transferable without retraining. Its new Section 4.5 acknowledges unresolved real-time performance and proposes combining the approach with distillation and deployment engineering. V1 instead includes explicit discussion of training from scratch and possible undertraining in Appendix C; whether those qualifications survive in v4's supplement is unknown.

D1.justification: V4 newly specifies a ten-day training time, 128×128 LR inputs for LSDIR-Test and RealSR, Y-channel PSNR/SSIM, the ManIQA-KONIQ model and wavelet color normalization. Its access statement changes from code and model being available to code becoming available. However, the missing supplement prevents matching v1's detailed architecture, classifier-training and encoder descriptions, leaving the overall extent of reproducibility changes uncertain.

R1.justification: V4 adds references including OSEDiff, MultiDiffusion, CAMixerSR and classification-based dynamic super-resolution, and connects the three-group design to earlier adaptive methods. Some older references, including SRCNN and EDSR, disappear from the reference list. The central positioning against uniform diffusion sampling remains substantially unchanged; SinSR was already cited in v1.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and much of the methodological and experimental prose are extensively rewritten. Retrieval receives a dedicated algorithm listing, the sampling section gains an extension subsection, and a discussion section enters the main narrative. Confidence notation changes from C* to Qmap. These are substantial explanatory and organizational revisions beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: V4 changes the paper to a two-column layout, merges v1's benchmark Tables 1–2, and replaces the sampling-configuration table with a multi-series plot. Figure 1 and the qualitative comparison are redesigned. Selected appendix confidence maps move into the main text with annotations, and the StableSR extension receives a new table and figure.

improvement.justification: The one-step baselines and StableSR transfer experiment strengthen evidence for efficiency and applicability, while the revised exposition makes several mechanisms clearer. However, v4's missing supplement prevents assessing whether v1's architectural documentation, supporting analyses and limitations are preserved. Higher reported scores also accompany changed training. These gaps prevent a reliable judgment of the net improvement in overall paper quality.
